brief.headline: Lock a 12–15% price cut to reach the ₹0.65–0.80/pc band typical for higher-volume PP caps, while qualifying Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a robust second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 12–15% reduction on rigid plastic packaging to bring us into the ₹0.65–0.80/pc range that the market allows at higher volumes and looser specs.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc (the lower band from the market ask)
priceAsk.basis: The open market for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap runs ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec. Our annual ₹44.37 L spend should qualify us for that higher-volume band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Push from 30 Days After Receipt to immediate payment on receipt, freeing up working cash for us.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹3.65 L of cash freed up for us by moving to immediate settlement (or ₹1.82 L if we move halfway to 15 days)

brief.financialLeverage: Rachana Plastics publishes no financials, so we cannot measure how healthy or cash-tight they are, or how much of their business our ₹44.37 L represents. That uncertainty means we lean on our own data and on backup options: we have five strong alternates — Manjushree (India's largest rigid-plastic converter, ₹2569.83 Cr, health B) and Mold-Tek (listed, ₹1010.97 Cr, health B) are the top two. With no visibility into Rachana's finances, we will lead by qualifying a robust second source and using the market's ₹0.65–0.80 band to anchor price, not by pressing on their cash position.

evidence.point: The open market for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volumes.
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc; typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc; headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: We spend ₹44.37 L a year with Rachana — enough volume to justify the lower market band.
HDPE resin import unit value sits at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a public benchmark for raw-material cost.
Moving from 30 Days After Receipt to immediate payment frees up ₹3.65 L in cash for us.
Manjushree — India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B — is a top second-source candidate for bottles and caps.
Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd — a listed rigid-plastic leader with revenue ₹1010.97 Cr and health score B — is another robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr, health B); proven pharma bottle and cap capability — the strongest second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr, health B); strong, profitable, with pharma containers and closures — a robust alternate.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging specialist (₹701.17 Cr, health C); broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Rachana publishes no financials — we cannot see if they are cash-tight or stable, so any hard push carries blind risk of destabilising a supplier we rely on for ₹44.37 L of packaging each year.
Without knowing how much of Rachana's revenue our ₹44.37 L represents, we cannot gauge how far we can push before triggering a walk-away or a quality cut.
The market-ask verdict is 'MARKET-FAIR' — our current pricing may already sit in the typical band (₹0.85–0.95/pc), so a 12–15% cut to ₹0.65–0.80 will require real volume or spec trade-offs.
Qualifying Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source will take 3–6 months of audits and trials — if Rachana senses urgency, our leverage shrinks.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're planning to dual-source rigid packaging this year, and we'd like Rachana to remain our lead partner — at a price that reflects the ₹0.65–0.80 band the market offers for our volumes.
